items.definition: The two cards the dealer gives a player face down at the start of a hand. They belong to that player alone. A player combines them with the board to make a five-card hand.
items.short_definition: The two private cards a player holds.

items.definition: The five cards the dealer puts face up in the middle of the table. Every player at the table shares the board and may use any of its cards.
items.short_definition: The five shared cards face up on the table.

items.definition: The top card of the pack, put face down to one side before the flop, the turn, and the river. A burn card takes no part in the hand and no player sees it.
items.short_definition: A card set aside face down before each new board card.

items.definition: The chips the players bet during a hand. The winner of the hand takes the pot. A player bets only the chips that sat on the table when the hand started.
items.short_definition: The chips the players compete for in one hand.

items.definition: A round disc that marks the seat counted as the dealer for one hand. It moves one seat clockwise after each hand. The button decides where the deal starts and where the action starts.
items.short_definition: The disc marking the nominal dealer seat.

items.definition: A forced bet two players put in the pot before they see any card. The player left of the button posts the small blind, and the next player posts the big blind.
items.short_definition: A forced bet posted before the deal.

items.definition: The place a player holds in the action order of a betting round. A player who acts late in the round already knows what the earlier players did.
items.short_definition: A player's place in the action order.

items.definition: The first three board cards. The dealer burns one card and turns all three face up together. A betting round follows.
items.short_definition: The first three board cards.

items.definition: The fourth board card. The dealer burns one card and turns it face up alone. A betting round follows.
items.short_definition: The fourth board card.

items.definition: The fifth and last board card. The dealer burns one card and turns it face up alone. The last betting round of the hand follows.
items.short_definition: The fifth and last board card.

items.definition: A check followed by a raise in the same betting round. A player checks, another player bets, and the first player then raises. The rules allow this play.
items.short_definition: A check, then a raise in the same round.

items.definition: A bet a player makes in more than one motion without stating the amount first. The dealer counts only the chips of the first motion.
items.short_definition: Chips pushed forward in more than one motion.

items.definition: The state of a player who put every remaining chip in the pot. An all-in player stays in the hand to the showdown but wins only the chips that player matched.
items.short_definition: Every remaining chip is in the pot.

items.definition: A pot built from the chips bet above an all-in amount. Only the players who put chips in that side pot may win it. The dealer builds one pot for each all-in level.
items.short_definition: A pot an all-in player cannot win.

items.definition: The point after the last betting round when two or more players remain. Those players turn their hole cards face up and compare hands, and the best hand takes the pot.
items.short_definition: The comparison of hands after the last bet.

items.definition: The pile of discarded cards beside the dealer. A hand that reaches the muck is dead and can win nothing. Players also use the word for the act of giving up a hand face down.
items.short_definition: The pile of discarded, dead cards.

items.definition: The highest card outside the ranked part of a hand. When two players hold the same rank of hand, the kicker decides the pot. Players compare kickers one at a time, highest first.
items.short_definition: The side card that breaks a tie.

items.definition: Five cards of one suit that run from ten up to the ace. It is the strongest hand in the game. Two royal flushes tie, and the pot then divides.
items.short_definition: Ten to ace, all in one suit.

items.definition: Five cards of one suit in an unbroken sequence. The highest card of the sequence decides which of two straight flushes wins.
items.short_definition: Five cards of one suit in sequence.

items.definition: Four cards of one rank plus one more card. The rank of the four cards decides which of two such hands wins.
items.short_definition: Four cards of the same rank.

items.definition: Three cards of one rank plus two cards of a second rank. The rank of the three cards decides the winner first. If those match, the rank of the pair decides.
items.short_definition: Three of one rank plus a pair.

items.definition: Five cards of one suit that do not form a sequence. Compare the highest card first, then the next highest. A suit never decides between two flushes.
items.short_definition: Five cards of one suit, out of sequence.

items.definition: Five cards in an unbroken sequence that do not all share one suit. The highest card of the sequence decides which of two straights wins.
items.short_definition: Five cards in sequence, mixed suits.

items.definition: Three cards of one rank plus two unmatched cards. The rank of the three cards decides the winner, and the two remaining cards then act as kickers.
items.short_definition: Three cards of the same rank.

items.definition: Two cards of one rank, two cards of a second rank, and one more card. Compare the higher pair first, then the lower pair, then the last card.
items.short_definition: Two separate pairs plus one card.

items.definition: Two cards of one rank plus three unmatched cards. Compare the rank of the pair first. If the pairs match, compare the three remaining cards in order.
items.short_definition: Two cards of the same rank.

items.definition: Five cards that match none of the higher ranks. The highest card decides, then the next highest, and so on through all five cards.
items.short_definition: No pair and no better rank.

items.definition: The strongest hand a player can hold on a given board. The board decides what the nuts is, and each new board card can change it.
items.short_definition: The best possible hand on this board.

items.definition: The action of putting chips in the pot when no player has bet in the round yet. In a no-limit game the smallest bet equals the big blind. The largest bet equals every chip the player holds on the table.
items.short_definition: Chips put in the pot when no bet stands.

items.definition: The action of putting in chips equal to the largest amount bet in the current round. The player stays in the hand. A player who already put chips in that round adds only the difference.
items.short_definition: Match the largest bet of the round.

items.definition: The action of putting in more than the amount needed to call. A raise reopens the round. Every other player must then call the new amount, raise again, or fold.
items.short_definition: Put in more than the amount needed to call.

items.definition: The action of giving up the hand and every claim to the pot. The player slides the two hole cards face down toward the dealer. Chips already in the pot stay in the pot.
items.short_definition: Give up the hand and the claim to the pot.

items.definition: The action of passing the turn without a bet. A player may check only when no bet stands in the current round. A check costs nothing and keeps the hand alive.
items.short_definition: Pass the turn without a bet.

items.definition: The smaller of the two forced bets posted before the deal. The player on the immediate left of the button posts it.
items.short_definition: The forced bet posted left of the button.

items.definition: The larger of the two forced bets posted before the deal. The next player clockwise from the small blind posts it, and it is normally twice the small blind. It counts as the first bet of the pre-flop round.
items.short_definition: The larger forced bet, and the first bet of the hand.

items.definition: The seat on the immediate left of the big blind. The player in that seat acts first before the flop.
items.short_definition: The seat that acts first before the flop.

items.definition: A small forced bet every player puts in the pot before the deal. It does not count toward the first bet of the round. The house or the tournament structure sets the size.
items.short_definition: A small forced bet from every player before the deal.

items.definition: The smallest legal raise. A raise must increase the current bet by at least the size of the last bet or the last raise in that round. Before the flop the big blind counts as that last bet.
items.short_definition: The smallest amount a legal raise may add.

items.definition: The rule that limits a player to the chips on the table when the hand starts. A player adds chips between hands and never during one. A player never takes chips off the table while a hand runs.
items.short_definition: A player bets only the chips on the table.

items.definition: A deal that goes wrong before real betting action starts. The dealer takes the cards back, shuffles the whole pack, and deals again with the button in the same seat.
items.short_definition: A faulty deal the dealer takes back.

items.definition: A hand that can win nothing. A hand dies when the player folds it or when it reaches the muck. It also dies when the player shows it to another player during the hand, or when it holds the wrong number of cards.
items.short_definition: A hand that can no longer win the pot.

items.definition: The fee the house takes out of the pot in a game played for cash. The dealer takes it before the winner receives the chips. The house sets the amount.
items.short_definition: The fee the house takes from the pot.

items.definition: The pot that holds the chips every player still in the hand matched, counted up to the size of the smallest all-in wager. Every player still in the hand may win it.
items.short_definition: The pot every remaining player may win.

items.definition: A pot that two or more hands of equal strength share in equal parts. If the pot does not divide evenly, the extra chip goes to the first tied player clockwise from the button.
items.short_definition: A pot that tied hands share.

items.definition: The first betting round. It starts as soon as every player holds two hole cards, and no board card is face up yet.
items.short_definition: The betting round before the flop.

items.definition: One of the four rounds in which the players bet. The four rounds run in this order: pre-flop, the flop, the turn, and the river.
items.short_definition: One of the four rounds of betting in a hand.

items.definition: The rule that the cards decide the winner at the showdown. The dealer reads every hand. A player who names the hand wrongly still wins when the cards hold the best hand.
items.short_definition: The cards decide the winner, not the words.

items.definition: The case in which a player's best five cards are the five board cards. That player uses no hole card. Every player who reaches the showdown holds at least the strength of the board.
items.short_definition: The five board cards are a player's best hand.

items.definition: A card the dealer turns face up by mistake. If one hole card goes face up during the deal, the dealer finishes the deal and gives that player the next card. The exposed card then becomes the burn card for the flop.
items.short_definition: A card the dealer turns face up by mistake.

items.definition: The supervisor who settles a dispute the players cannot settle. The floor puts a fair game and the best interest of the whole table first, and the ruling stands for that hand.
items.short_definition: The supervisor who settles a dispute.

items.definition: The price a player pays to enter a tournament. Every player pays the same price and starts with the same number of chips.
items.short_definition: The price of entry to a tournament.

items.definition: A period of a tournament in which the blinds hold one size. The blinds rise at set times, and each new level raises the cost of a hand.
items.short_definition: A period of a tournament with one blind size.

items.definition: A hand with only two players in it. The player on the button posts the small blind and acts first before the flop. The other player acts first on every later round.
items.short_definition: A hand with only two players.

items.definition: An action a player takes before their own turn. The action does not bind the player if the action in front of that player changes. If nothing changes, the dealer holds the player to it.
items.short_definition: An action taken before a player's turn.

items.definition: One chip worth more than the amount needed to call. A player who puts it in with no spoken raise has called, and the dealer returns the difference.
items.short_definition: One chip worth more than the call.

items.definition: A clear statement a player makes at their own turn. The statement binds that player. A player who says a raise to 500 must put 500 in the pot.
items.short_definition: A statement at a player's turn binds that player.

items.definition: The straight five, four, three, two, ace. The ace runs low in this sequence, so the five is the highest card of it.
items.short_definition: The straight from five down to the ace.

items.definition: The choice the big blind holds when no player raises before the action returns to that seat. The big blind may then check or raise.
items.short_definition: The big blind's choice to check or raise.

items.definition: The rule that a player plays the hand alone. A player takes no advice about a live hand, and shows the hole cards to nobody while the hand runs.
items.short_definition: A player plays the hand without help.
